comment: Topic-specific management steps (NICE-based). Key = lowercase keyword match in tool title. First match wins.

options.label: 140–160/90–100 mmHg
options.guidance: Lifestyle advice; offer antihypertensive if CVD risk ≥10% (QRISK3) or end-organ damage. First-line: ACE-i or ARB (or CCB if >55 or Afro-Caribbean). Target <140/90 (diabetes/CKD: <130/80). NICE NG136.

options.label: ≥160/100 mmHg
options.guidance: Start drug treatment; two agents if >160/100. First-line: ACE-i + CCB (or thiazide if CCB not tolerated). A/B blockers not first-line. Confirm with ABPM/HBPM. NICE NG136.

options.label: Resistant (3 drugs at best dose)
options.guidance: Add spironolactone 25 mg if K+ ≤4.5. Exclude non-adherence, white-coat, secondary causes (renal, endocrine). Consider specialist. NICE NG136.

options.label: New treatment
options.guidance: Review in 4–6 weeks; titrate to target. Then 6-monthly then annual. Check U&E before and after ACE-i/ARB; K+ before spironolactone. NICE NG136.

options.label: Stable on treatment
options.guidance: Annual BP, creatinine, K+, lipids; CVD risk every 5 years. Reinforce lifestyle. NICE NG136.

options.label: Regular, no red flags
options.guidance: History: triggers, duration. Check FBC, U&E, TFT. Consider 24h tape if intermittent. Reassure if benign; treat anxiety if relevant. NICE NG196.

options.label: Irregular or suspected AF
options.guidance: ECG (or rhythm strip). If AF: assess stroke risk (CHA2DS2-Vasc), bleeding (HAS-BLED), rate/rhythm control. Anticoagulate per NICE NG196. Refer if haemodynamically unstable or first confirmed AF for consideration of rhythm control.

options.label: Red flags (syncope, chest pain, SOB)
options.guidance: ECG urgently. Consider same-day referral or ambulance if syncope, chest pain, or severe SOB. Exclude VT, heart block, PE. NICE NG196.

options.label: Suspected COPD
options.guidance: Spirometry (post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC <0.7). Staging by FEV1%. Assess breathlessness (MRC), exacerbations. Exclude asthma. NICE NG115.

options.label: Stable COPD – step-up
options.guidance: Step 1: SABA prn. Step 2: add LABA or LAMA. Step 3: LABA+LAMA. Step 4: add ICS if eosinophils ≥0.3 or ≥2 exacerbations/year. Offer pulmonary rehab. NICE NG115.

options.label: Acute exacerbation
options.guidance: Prednisolone 30 mg 7–14 days. Antibiotic if purulent sputum: doxycycline or amoxicillin (or clarithromycin). Increase bronchodilators. Consider hospital if severe. NICE NG115.

options.label: Step 1 – SABA only
options.guidance: Intermittent asthma: SABA prn. If using SABA ≥3/week or symptoms ≥3/week or night waking: add low-dose ICS (step 2). NICE NG80.

options.label: Step 2–3 – ICS ± LABA
options.guidance: Step 2: low-dose ICS. Step 3: add LABA (continue ICS). If good control on low ICS+LABA, consider trial of LABA withdrawal. NICE NG80.

options.label: Step 4–5 – add-on
options.guidance: Step 4: increase ICS to MART or add LTRA/ LAMA. Step 5: add prednisolone or refer. Check technique, adherence, consider occupational. NICE NG80.

options.label: New T2DM
options.guidance: HbA1c target 48 mmol/mol (6.5%) or individualise. First-line: metformin. Add SGLT2i if CVD/HF/CKD; otherwise add DPP-4i, SU, or GLP-1 (if BMI ≥35 or need weight). NICE NG28.

options.label: Intensification
options.guidance: Dual therapy: metformin + SGLT2i (if CVD/HF/CKD/weight) or DPP-4i/SU/GLP-1. Triple therapy as per NG28. Consider GLP-1 if BMI ≥35 and need weight loss. NICE NG28.

options.label: Monitoring
options.guidance: HbA1c 3–6 monthly until stable then 6-monthly. Annual: lipids, U&E, eGFR, BP, weight, feet, eyes (retinopathy). NICE NG28.

options.label: Mild
options.guidance: Watchful waiting, active monitoring, or psychological intervention (CBT, exercise). Do not offer antidepressant as first-line. NICE NG222.

options.label: Moderate
options.guidance: SSRI (e.g. sertraline) or psychological intervention. Review at 2 weeks; continue 6 months after remission. NICE NG222.

options.label: Severe or treatment-resistant
options.guidance: Combination antidepressant + high-intensity psychological therapy. Consider referral. Risk assess; consider crisis if suicidal. NICE NG222.

options.label: Mild
options.guidance: Psychological intervention (CBT) or self-help. Consider SSRI if declining or not improving. NICE NG226.

options.label: Moderate or severe
options.guidance: SSRI (sertraline first-line) or psychological therapy. Review at 2 weeks. Continue 6–12 months after remission. NICE NG226.

options.label: Uncomplicated lower UTI
options.guidance: Nitrofurantoin 100 mg MR bd 3 days (avoid if eGFR <45), or trimethoprim 200 mg bd 3 days (check resistance), or pivmecillinam. Send MSU if recurrent or pyelonephritis. NICE NG109.

options.label: Pyelonephritis
options.guidance: Send MSU. Oral: cefalexin or co-amoxiclav 7–10 days. Admit if systemically unwell, pregnant, or not improving. NICE NG109.

options.label: Recurrent UTI
options.guidance: Consider prophylaxis (nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim at night) or post-coital. Exclude structural cause. NICE NG109.

options.label: No red flags
options.guidance: Advise stay active; paracetamol + NSAID short-term. Consider manual therapy. Do not offer imaging. Review at 6 weeks. NICE NG59.

options.label: Red flags (cauda equina, fracture, infection)
options.guidance: Cauda equina: emergency referral. Consider fracture if trauma/steroids; infection if fever. MRI if nerve root compression suspected for surgical option. NICE NG59.

options.label: Acute attack
options.guidance: NSAID (e.g. naproxen) + PPI, or colchicine 500 mcg bd–qd (max 6 mg per attack), or prednisolone 30 mg 3–5 days. Start within 24 h. NICE NG219.

options.label: Urate-lowering (recurrent or tophi)
options.guidance: Allopurinol 100 mg daily, titrate to target sUA <300 µmol/L. Prophylaxis: colchicine or NSAID for first 6 months. NICE NG219.

options.label: Suspected HF
options.guidance: BNP or NT-proBNP. If raised: echo. Refer for echo if very high or urgent. NICE NG106.

options.label: HFrEF (LVEF ≤40%)
options.guidance: ACE-i (or ARNI) + beta-blocker + MRA. Add SGLT2i (dapagliflozin/empagliflozin). Titrate to target. NICE NG106.

options.label: HFpEF
options.guidance: Treat comorbidities (BP, AF, diabetes). Diuretics for congestion. No routine ACE-i for HFpEF alone. NICE NG106.

options.label: TSH >10
options.guidance: Overt hypothyroidism. Start levothyroxine 25–50 mcg OD (lower if elderly/cardiac). Recheck TSH in 6–8 weeks; titrate to TSH 0.4–2.0. NICE NG145.

options.label: TSH 4.5–10, normal T4
options.guidance: Check TPO antibodies. Consider trial of levothyroxine if symptomatic or TPO+ or TSH >10. NICE NG145.

options.label: TSH <0.1 / hyperthyroid
options.guidance: Check T4/T3. Refer endocrinology (Graves, nodule, thyroiditis). If on levothyroxine: reduce dose. NICE NG145.

options.label: Mild
options.guidance: Emollients liberally. Mild topical steroid (e.g. hydrocortisone 1%) for flares short-term. Avoid triggers. NICE NG80 (CKS Eczema).

options.label: Moderate
options.guidance: Moderate potency topical steroid (e.g. betamethasone 0.025%) for flares. Consider bandaging. Step down when controlled. NICE NG80.

options.label: Severe or not controlled
options.guidance: Potent topical steroid or referral for phototherapy/ systemic. Exclude infection. Consider patch testing. NICE NG80.

options.label: Primary prevention, QRISK3 ≥10%
options.guidance: Offer atorvastatin 20 mg (or simvastatin 40 mg if atorvastatin not tolerated). Discuss lifestyle. Recheck lipids in 3 months. NICE NG238.

options.label: Primary prevention, high risk
options.guidance: Consider higher intensity (atorvastatin 80 mg) if QRISK3 ≥10% and lifestyle addressed. NICE NG238.

options.label: Secondary prevention
options.guidance: High-intensity statin (atorvastatin 80 mg). Aim LDL reduction >40%. Add ezetimibe if not at target. NICE NG238.

options.label: Score 0–1 (no antibiotic)
options.guidance: Paracetamol/NSAID. No antibiotic. Safety-net: if worsening or no improvement in 1 week, re-assess. NICE NG84.

options.label: Score 2–3
options.guidance: Back-up or immediate antibiotic: phenoxymethylpenicillin 500 mg qds 5–10 days (or clarithromycin if penicillin allergic). NICE NG84.

options.label: Score 4–5
options.guidance: Immediate antibiotic. Consider throat swab. Penicillin 10 days. NICE NG84.

options.label: Mild, no systemic illness
options.guidance: Safety-netting; paracetamol/ibuprofen. Most resolve in 3 days. No antibiotic first-line. NICE NG91.

options.label: Systemically unwell or high risk
options.guidance: Amoxicillin 5–7 days (or erythromycin if penicillin allergic). Consider if <2 years bilateral, or otorrhoea. NICE NG91.

options.label: Likely viral (<10 days)
options.guidance: Paracetamol/NSAID. No antibiotic. Advise if no improvement by 10 days or worsening, re-assess. NICE NG79.

options.label: Persistent or severe
options.guidance: Consider phenoxymethylpenicillin or co-amoxiclav 7 days if no improvement after 10 days or severe. NICE NG79.

options.label: First-line
options.guidance: Increase fibre, fluids, activity. Consider bulk-forming (e.g. ispaghula). NICE NG99.

options.label: Osmotic / stimulant
options.guidance: Osmotic: macrogol. Stimulant: senna or bisacodyl short-term. Avoid long-term stimulant. NICE NG99.

options.label: Lifestyle and antacid
options.guidance: Weight loss, smaller meals, avoid triggers. Alginate or antacid prn. NICE NG1.

options.label: PPI
options.guidance: Full-dose PPI 4–8 weeks (e.g. omeprazole 20 mg OD). Step down to lowest dose that controls. NICE NG1.

options.label: Dysphagia / alarm
options.guidance: Refer for endoscopy: dysphagia, weight loss, haematemesis, >55 with new dyspepsia. NICE NG1.

options.label: Acute migraine
options.guidance: Triptan + NSAID (or paracetamol). Anti-emetic if nausea. Avoid opiates. NICE NG150.

options.label: Prophylaxis (≥8 days/month)
options.guidance: Propranolol or topiramate. Consider referral if not controlled. NICE NG150.

options.label: Tension-type
options.guidance: Paracetamol or NSAID. Address stress, posture. Avoid frequent analgesia (medication-overuse). NICE NG150.

options.label: No uterus – oestrogen only
options.guidance: Oestrogen only (patch/gel preferred for VTE risk). Review annually. NICE NG23.

options.label: With uterus – combined
options.guidance: Oestrogen + cyclical or continuous progestogen. Sequential if perimenopausal; continuous if postmenopausal. NICE NG23.

options.label: Contraindications / alternatives
options.guidance: Contraindications: breast cancer, VTE, stroke. Consider non-hormonal (clonidine, CBT) or topical oestrogen for urogenital. NICE NG23.

options.label: G3a (eGFR 45–59)
options.guidance: Confirm with repeat; address CV risk, BP (target <130/80 if diabetic/proteinuric). Avoid nephrotoxics. NICE NG203.

options.label: G3b–4 (eGFR 15–44)
options.guidance: Monitor 6–12 monthly. Anaemia, bone, K+. Refer if eGFR <30 or rapid decline. Consider SGLT2i if T2DM. NICE NG203.

options.label: G5 (eGFR <15)
options.guidance: Refer nephrology. Plan for RRT. Manage complications. NICE NG203.

options.label: Mild (comedones)
options.guidance: Topical: adapalene 0.1% or benzoyl peroxide 5% OD. If inadequate after 12 weeks add topical antibiotic (e.g. clindamycin). NICE NG198.

options.label: Moderate (inflammatory)
options.guidance: Fixed combination: adapalene + benzoyl peroxide, or topical abx + benzoyl peroxide. If inadequate: oral doxycycline 100 mg OD 12 weeks (or lymecycline). NICE NG198.

options.label: Severe or scarring
options.guidance: Refer dermatology for oral isotretinoin. Exclude pregnancy; contraception. Do not offer oral antibiotic long-term as monotherapy. NICE NG198.

options.label: Mild (no systemic features)
options.guidance: Oral flucloxacillin 500 mg qds 7 days (or clarithromycin 500 mg bd if penicillin allergic). Elevate limb. Review at 48 h. NICE NG141.

options.label: Moderate (fever, spreading)
options.guidance: Oral co-amoxiclav 500/125 mg tds 7 days, or flucloxacillin + phenoxymethylpenicillin. Consider IV if not improving. NICE NG141.

options.label: Severe / orbital / facial
options.guidance: Admit for IV benzylpenicillin or flucloxacillin. 2WW not appropriate; emergency assessment. NICE NG141.

options.label: Stroke prevention
options.guidance: CHA2DS2-VASc ≥2 (men) or ≥3 (women): offer anticoagulation. DOAC preferred (apixaban 5 mg bd, rivaroxaban 20 mg OD, edoxaban, dabigatran). Warfarin if DOAC unsuitable. HAS-BLED for bleeding risk. NICE NG196.

options.label: Rate control
options.guidance: Beta-blocker (bisoprolol) or rate-limiting CCB (diltiazem). Digoxin if sedentary. Target resting HR <110 (or <80 if symptomatic). NICE NG196.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance: Refer cardiology: first confirmed AF, for rhythm control or ablation; young; haemodynamically unstable. Emergency if severe haemodynamic compromise. NICE NG196.

options.label: Wells score – likely DVT
options.guidance: D-dimer if Wells 1–2; if positive or Wells ≥3 do proximal leg USS. If DVT confirmed: anticoagulate. NICE NG158.

options.label: Confirmed DVT – anticoagulation
options.guidance: DOAC (apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban) or warfarin. Apixaban 10 mg bd 7 days then 5 mg bd. Minimum 3 months; extend if unprovoked or ongoing risk. NICE NG158.

options.label: Suspected PE
options.guidance: Wells PE; D-dimer (if low clinical probability); if positive CTPA. Treat as per NG158. Admit if haemodynamically unstable.

options.label: CURB65 0–1 (home)
options.guidance: Oral amoxicillin 500 mg tds 5 days (or doxycycline 200 mg stat then 100 mg OD if penicillin allergic). Safety-net. NICE NG138.

options.label: CURB65 2
options.guidance: Consider hospital; if home: oral amoxicillin 1 g tds or co-amoxiclav. Consider co-amoxiclav if atypical suspected. NICE NG138.

options.label: CURB65 ≥3
options.guidance: Admit. IV co-amoxiclav or benzylpenicillin + clarithromycin. NICE NG138.

options.label: Iron deficiency
options.guidance: Ferrous sulfate 200 mg OD or bd (or ferrous fumarate). Recheck Hb in 2–4 weeks. Continue 3 months after normal. If not responding: check compliance, consider malabsorption, 2WW if red flags. NICE NG24.

options.label: B12 deficiency
options.guidance: Hydroxocobalamin 1 mg IM 3× per week 2 weeks then 1 mg every 3 months (or oral if mild and compliant). Check folate. NICE NG241.

options.label: Macrocytic (B12/folate)
options.guidance: Check B12 and folate. Treat as above. If both normal consider alcohol, hypothyroid, MDS – consider referral. NICE NG24.

options.label: Suspected new RA
options.guidance: 2WW rheumatology if persistent synovitis. Check RF, anti-CCP, CRP, FBC, U&E, LFT. Start DMARD within 3 months. NICE NG100.

options.label: DMARD choice
options.guidance: First-line: methotrexate 15 mg weekly (folic acid 5 mg weekly). Add sulfasalazine or hydroxychloroquine if MTX incomplete. Monitor FBC, LFT, creatinine. NICE NG100.

options.label: Acute flare
options.guidance: Short-term prednisolone (e.g. 15 mg OD reducing over 3 weeks). Do not use long-term steroid without DMARD. NICE NG100.

options.label: Core treatment
options.guidance: Exercise, weight loss if overweight. Paracetamol prn. Topical NSAID (e.g. ibuprofen gel) for knee/hand. NICE NG226.

options.label: Oral NSAID
options.guidance: Oral NSAID at lowest dose (e.g. ibuprofen 400 mg tds) + PPI. Use short-term. Avoid if CKD, high CV risk. Consider topical first for knee. NICE NG226.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance: Consider referral for joint replacement if severe impact despite non-surgical treatment. NICE NG226.

options.label: First-line
options.guidance: Diet: fibre, low FODMAP trial. Avoid trigger foods. Antispasmodic (e.g. mebeverine 135 mg tds or hyoscine). NICE NG61.

options.label: IBS-D
options.guidance: Loperamide prn. Consider trial of low-dose amitriptyline (10 mg) if refractory. NICE NG61.

options.label: IBS-C
options.guidance: Linaclotide 290 mcg OD if inadequate response to laxatives. NICE NG61.

options.label: Diagnosis
options.guidance: IgA TTG + total IgA. If positive refer for duodenal biopsy. Do not start gluten-free diet before biopsy. NICE NG20.

options.label: Management
options.guidance: Lifelong gluten-free diet. Dietitian referral. Annual review: Hb, B12, folate, ferritin, TFT, bone. NICE NG20.

options.label: Refractory
options.guidance: Refer gastroenterology if symptoms persist despite strict GFD. Exclude lymphoma. NICE NG20.

options.label: Uncomplicated
options.guidance: High-fibre diet. Avoid routine antibiotics. Bulk-forming laxative if constipation. NICE NG147.

options.label: Acute diverticulitis
options.guidance: Mild: oral co-amoxiclav or ciprofloxacin + metronidazole 5–7 days. Clear fluids if severe. Admit if systemically unwell, peritonism, or not improving. NICE NG147.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance: Refer if recurrent attacks, complications (abscess, fistula, stricture), or diagnostic uncertainty. NICE NG147.

options.label: Fever + non-blanching rash
options.guidance: Treat as meningococcal disease until proved otherwise. Immediate parenteral antibiotic (ceftriaxone or benzylpenicillin). Emergency admission. NICE NG51.

options.label: No fever, well child
options.guidance: Consider ITP, HSP. FBC, clotting. Refer paediatrics if unwell or platelets <20. NICE CKS.

options.label: Suspected melanoma
options.guidance: 2WW dermatology. Do not excise in primary care. ABCDE criteria; any changing mole or ulcerated lesion. NICE NG14.

options.label: Suspected BCC
options.guidance: Routine referral or minor surgery if appropriate. NICE NG12.

options.label: Suspected SCC
options.guidance: 2WW. Urgent if high risk (size, site, immunosuppression). NICE NG12.

options.label: Standard
options.guidance: Permethrin 5% cream: apply to whole body (neck down), leave 8–12 h, repeat after 7 days. Treat all household contacts. Wash bedding. CKS Scabies.

options.label: Crusted
options.guidance: Refer dermatology. Ivermectin (unlicensed) or permethrin under supervision. CKS Scabies.

options.label: Acute TIA (ABCD2 ≥4 or crescendo)
options.guidance: Same-day specialist assessment. Aspirin 300 mg immediately then 75 mg OD. NICE NG128.

options.label: Secondary prevention
options.guidance: Antiplatelet: clopidogrel 75 mg OD (or aspirin + dipyridamole). BP and lipid targets. Consider anticoagulation if AF. NICE NG128.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance: All TIAs: urgent referral for investigation (imaging, carotid). NICE NG128.

options.label: First seizure
options.guidance: Refer neurologist (2WW). Do not drive until assessed. EEG and MRI. NICE NG217.

options.label: Drug choice
options.guidance: First-line: levetiracetam, lamotrigine, or carbamazepine (depending on seizure type). Monotherapy; titrate. NICE NG217.

options.label: Pregnancy
options.guidance: High-dose folic acid 5 mg. Review drugs (valproate avoid). Specialist advice. NICE NG217.

options.label: Visible haematuria (any age)
options.guidance: Refer urology 2WW. Exclude UTI; if UTI treat and repeat urine. NICE NG12.

options.label: Non-visible (≥45)
options.guidance: FBC, U&E, eGFR. Refer 2WW if eGFR <60 or other concern. Otherwise routine referral for cystoscopy/imaging. NICE NG12.

options.label: Medical management
options.guidance: Alpha-blocker (tamsulosin 400 mcg OD) for flow. 5-alpha reductase inhibitor (finasteride 5 mg) if enlarged prostate. Combination if both. NICE NG97.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance: Refer urology: retention, recurrent UTI, stones, renal impairment, failed medical treatment, or suspected cancer. NICE NG97.

options.label: NRT
options.guidance: Nicotine patch + short-acting (gum/lozenge) for cravings. 8–12 weeks. Adjust dose by smoking level. NICE NG92.

options.label: Varenicline
options.guidance: Varenicline 500 mcg OD 3 days, then 1 mg bd 12 weeks. Start 1–2 weeks before quit date. NICE NG92.

options.label: Bupropion
options.guidance: Bupropion 150 mg OD 6 days then 150 mg bd 7–9 weeks. Contraindicated in seizure, eating disorder. NICE NG92.

options.label: Green (low risk)
options.guidance: Paracetamol/ibuprofen for distress. Safety-net: red/amber features, no improvement 48 h. NICE NG143.

options.label: Amber (intermediate)
options.guidance: Clinical assessment. Consider urine dip, FBC, CRP. Refer if no focus or concern. NICE NG143.

options.label: Red (high risk)
options.guidance: Emergency admission. Meningococcal, sepsis, or dehydrated. NICE NG143.
